QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_19

question.text: To mitigate concentration risk, SEBI caps single-investee-company exposure for Category I and II AIFs at what percentage of the AUM or investable funds, directly or through units of other AIFs?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 7.2 (Concentration Risk) and SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012: Category I and II AIFs cannot invest more than 25% of AUM or investable funds in one investee company, directly or through investment in units of other AIFs. (Cat III has a separate 10% cap). The Trap: 10% is the Cat III limit — tempting XIX-B trap. 15% is fictitious. 50% is the large-value-fund relaxation for certain underlying concentration — not the default. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B covers the 10% Cat III cap. XIX-C must distinguish 25% Cat I/II vs 10% Cat III. XIX-A distributors need to explain the cap to HNI LPs.
